newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks end day firmer, U.S. data supports.
newsitem.headline: German stocks end day firmer, U.S. data supports.

text.p: German shares ended trade on Friday modestly higher, encouraged by weaker-than-expected U.S. September producer price data, but the market stayed short of record highs reached at the beginning of the week.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings in the DAX, ended 9.17 points, or 0.34 percent, higher at 2,692.69, off a day's high of 2,700.36 touched after the release of the U.S. figures.

Before the numbers came out, the DAX index of 30 blue chip shares closed at 2,686.03, gaining 5.28 points or 0.20 percent. "The tone for next week will be set by how the U.S. reacts to this data," said one dealer.
Dealers said more data out of the U.S. next Wednesday would keep the focus across the Atlantic.
In particular, U.S. September consumer prices will be eagerly awaited for a clearer indication of the inflation outlook for the country.
Some dealers said the DAX was still in a consolidation phase after a spate of record highs, while others said the index needs a downward correction, before it can climb further.
Chemicals company Hoechst made strides at the end of IBIS trading after its blood pressure drug gained approval in the U.S.. It ended computer dealings 1.08 marks, or nearly two percent, up at 58.39.
Car maker Daimler-Benz also climbed in late computer trade after JP Morgan Securities started coverage of the company, recommending a buy on the stock.
Daimler, the most heavily-traded share on IBIS during the day, ended electronic dealings up 79 pfennigs at 83.69 marks.
Construction group Philipp Holzmann AG rose 19 marks, or over five percent, to 364 marks in late IBIS trade, after forecasting it would break even in the current business year.

After climbing earlier in the week on news of a telecoms deal, traders said utilities firms RWE and Veba suffered from some profit-taking. RWE was off 24 pfennigs at 60.92 marks and Veba lost 26 pfennigs to drop to 82.10 marks at the end of IBIS trade.
